name: Doublo HIFU

lead: Doublo is a Korean-made intense focused ultrasound (HIFU) device used to tighten facial and neck skin without surgery.

Focused ultrasound heats tissue at various depths below the surface while sparing the surface layer, prompting collagen remodeling and tightening. Two small studies in Asian patients have been published: a 2015 study of 11 patients on histologic change, safety and efficacy, and a 2020 study of 43 patients on neck and lower-face laxity whose authors described good safety but limited efficacy.

paras: It is used in clinics by trained providers as an in-office session aimed at mild-to-moderate laxity of the lower face and neck. Changes, where they occur, develop gradually over weeks to months.
The 2020 study describes IFUS as having a good safety profile. Details beyond that were not available in the reviewed sources.

angle.text: Doublo is a Korean HIFU device used for facial and neck skin tightening. Focused ultrasound heats deep tissue and prompts collagen remodeling. Two small published studies in Asian patients have examined it, one reporting limited efficacy.

lead: Doublo is an intense focused ultrasound (IFUS, also called HIFU) device made by HIRONIC Co. of Seongnam, Korea, used for noninvasive facial and neck skin tightening.[1] Two published studies in Asian patients have examined it.[1][2]

A 2015 study of 11 patients assessed histologic changes, safety and efficacy, and a 2020 prospective study of 43 patients reported the authors' experience treating neck and lower-face laxity.[1][2] The latter paper describes IFUS as having a good safety profile but limited efficacy, with most earlier research having used the Ulthera system.[2]

paras: IFUS produces thermal effects at various depths while sparing overlying tissue, and is used for skin laxity.[1] The 2020 paper characterises it as nonablative.[2]

A 2015 study treated eleven patients (mean age 46) with facial laxity and compared them before and after treatment, including histology.[1] A 2020 prospective study of 43 patients with neck and lower-face laxity reported results with the Doublo device.[2] A registered trial (NCT04157218, status unknown) planned to compare thread lifting and microfocused ultrasound in 45 participants.[3]

timeline.event: Histologic study of Doublo in 11 patients published.[1]
